items.fact: The bit depth of Kinetix_red was not measured. The dia-lamp frame at 500 ms reached a maximum of 861 ADU on one pixel (saturated fraction 3.5e-7) and did not saturate. The run log's 'bits: 10' at this event is a flaw in the script, which did not test for saturation; it is not a bit depth. The brightest pixel seen today was about 13,990 ADU, in the particle series, so full scale is above that.

items.fact: pymmcore-plus 0.18.1's CMMCorePlus.instance() holds its singleton weakly: when the last strong reference is dropped the core is destroyed, and destroying a core unloads every device. A later instance() returns a new empty core, whose getLoadedDevices() still lists 'Core'. Code must keep its own strong reference to a loaded core.
items.how: run-20260924-001 loaded all devices and failed 16 ms later with 'No device with label' (its event 12); the core log showed 'Did unload all devices ... Core session ended' right after the load; reproduced without hardware by dropping the reference and collecting. The fix and its account are commit 0d94690, and the file below carries the reason.

items.fact: Under continuous Aura GREEN at 100 per-mille for 300 s (20x, one 100 ms frame per second, 300 frames, fresh field), total particle fluorescence (sum over the whole frame of pixels more than 300 ADU above the frame median, dark subtracted) ended at 100.7% of the first frame and stayed between 100% and about 103.5% throughout. items.fact: In the fresh field of run-20260924-006 the roughly 30 particles moved during the five minutes: nearest-neighbour displacement from frame 0 was a median 7 px (max 29 px) after 60 s and a median 17 px (max 37 px) after 299 s, with 73% moving more than 10 px. At 20x that is several micrometres. Whether it is stage drift, sample flow or free particles was not separated. Any per-particle or fixed-mask brightness over time on this sample needs tracking.
